log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Bring Garchomp (Mega), Gholdengo, and Dragapult for speed and power. Opponent has a mirror team. Garchomp's Mega Evolution should outspeed most of their team. Beware their Kingambit's Sucker Punch and their Incineroar's Fake Out.

Turn 1: Mirror Garchomp lead. Dragon Claw is super effective on it. I plan to Mega Evolve (Mega Garchomp is slower-ish but stronger). Opponent items and moves are unknown. Watch for their Kingambit's Sucker Punch and their Incineroar's Fake Out.

Mirror Garchomp fight. Both Mega Garchomps are at the same speed (158), so it's a coin flip who moves first. Mine is at 23 HP and theirs at 17%, so Dragon Claw wins if I move first. Dragapult (Spe 213) and Gholdengo (scarf, 149) are in reserve. Watch for their Kingambit's Sucker Punch and their Incineroar's Fake Out.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Both Garchomps are mirrors with the same 158 Speed spread, so this is essentially a speed tie—since the opponent moved first with Dragon Claw, they must have won that coin flip this turn, even though my Garchomp is in much better shape at 23 HP versus their 17%.

Given the mirror matchup, I could switch to Gholdengo for a resist, but Earthquake punches through that since it's weak to Ground. Dragapult outspeeds cleanly but eats a hit coming in. Really, my best play is just firing Dragon Claw myself: it's super effective and has a fair shot at winning the speed tie outright, and since my Garchomp is already low, the risk of losing the tie costs little compared to the upside of cleanly knocking out their last-legs Garchomp.

decisions.thought: Mirror Garchomp lost. Their Mega Garchomp is at 17%, Spe about 158. Gholdengo (scarf, Spe 223) should outspeed it and finish it with Make It Rain. Dragapult (Spe 213) is the backup. Watch for their Kingambit Sucker Punch and Incineroar Fake Out.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Checking speed and typing matchups: my scarfed Gholdengo outspeeds their Mega Garchomp, and while Dragon-type moves are resisted by its Steel typing, Earthquake would hit it super effectively since Ground is neutral against Ghost but strong against Steel.

Either Gholdengo or Dragapult could outspeed and score the kill on the weakened Garchomp, but since my pokemon just fainted I get a free switch-in before the opponent attacks again. I'll go with Gholdengo since it outspeeds reliably and Make It Rain hits neutrally, saving Dragapult's life orb option for later.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo has a Choice Scarf (Spe 223 with the scarf), which should outspeed their Mega Garchomp (Spe up to 158). Use Shadow Ball to finish it, since it avoids the Make It Rain SpA drop. Backup is Dragapult (Life Orb, Spe 213). Watch for Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Incineroar's Fake Out.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Choice Scarf, Gholdengo's speed jumps well past 158, so it outspeeds everything here. Garchomp is at 17% and Steel-type Make It Rain hits neutrally, so it should kill easily, though I'll be locked into that move afterward with the SpA drop.

Actually Shadow Ball also kills the 17% chomp cleanly with its SpA stat, and avoids the Make It Rain SpA drop lock-in. Shadow Ball is resisted by Dark/Steel types like Kingambit but hits most of the relevant threats neutrally, so it's the safer lock-in choice here.

decisions.thought: Turn 4: Their Garchomp is down. Gholdengo (Choice Scarf) is locked into Shadow Ball, which Incineroar resists, so I switch to Dragapult (Life Orb, Spe 213) and use Dracometeor. Their last Pokémon is one of kingambit, gholdengo, dragapult or corviknight. Watch for Fake Out and Knock Off from Incineroar, and Sucker Punch from Kingambit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm working through type matchups—Gholdengo locked into Shadow Ball would be weak against Incineroar since Dark resists Ghost, so that matchup doesn't favor Gholdengo here.

Switching to Dragapult looks better since it outspeeds Incineroar and can hit hard with Draco Meteor, while Flamethrower gets resisted; it does risk taking a hit on switch-in, but breaking Gholdengo's scarf lock seems worthwhile. I'll switch to Dragapult.

decisions.thought: Turn 5: Dragapult (Life Orb, Spe 213) outspeeds Incineroar. Dracometeor is its best damage, roughly 45%. Flare Blitz hits Dragapult for only about 56 because Fire is resisted. Gholdengo (scarf) is weak to Fire, so keep it in reserve. Their last Pokémon is unknown. Watch for Sucker Punch from Kingambit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm calculating Dracometeor's damage from Dragapult against Incineroar, working through the base power, special attack, and Life Orb multiplier to estimate the percentage dealt.

So it's roughly 45% off a non-KO hit, leaving Incineroar to retaliate with a resisted Flare Blitz that Dragapult can tank. I'm also weighing whether U-turning into Gholdengo is safer, but Flare Blitz hits Gholdengo's Steel typing super effectively, so that's risky. Sticking with Dracometeor and absorbing the recoil-weakened Flare Blitz afterward seems like the better line.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Spe 149) outspeeds Incineroar. Thunderbolt is its best neutral damage, since Shadow Ball and Make It Rain are both resisted. Incineroar is at 62% and has Flare Blitz and Darkest Lariat. Their last Pokémon is unknown: kingambit, gholdengo, dragapult or corviknight.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo's Choice Scarf lock reset after switching, so it's not committed to Shadow Ball anymore. Incineroar at 62% is weak to Fire moves since Shadow Ball is resisted by its Dark typing and Make It Rain is resisted by Fire—Thunderbolt stays neutral, but Flare Blitz from Incineroar would hit Gholdengo hard.

Two Thunderbolts should roughly add up against Incineroar's HP, so it's a reasonably close but workable trade, and being locked into Thunderbolt isn't a big downside since it stays neutral-to-good against the likely remaining threats like Corviknight, Dragapult, and Kingambit. I'll go with Thunderbolt.
